mentions.text: Almost everyone will say they're huge music fans, enjoying music is probably one of the most common shared human experiences. But in there are vastly different levels of how "into it" people really are. Now obviously this is true for a lot of things, where there are casual fans and people who are more into it as a serious hobby. But for music there is a significant amount of people who will say that they're huge music fans that in reality have extremely shallow knowledge of the music scene, even of the artist that they're fans of. "I'm a huge country fan Chris Stapleton is my favorite singer" you ask what they thought of his latest album from the other year and get back a " Oh I don't know but Tennessee Whiskey is my favorite song." It's the people who used to mostly just put on top 40 radio, who now probably just have 5 or 6 spotify or youtube algorithm curated playlists saved that they listen on repeat. Now, I don't mean to invalidate people's experience and I don't want to push some elitist takes on "being a real music fan". It's perfectly fine to listen to music without making it an active hobby. But the last time I saw a discussion on AI music here some people were saying thin

mentions.text: If we're using the example of jazz song about watering plants, then I may perhaps consider that devoid of effort. I think my opinion is fluid when it comes to prompt related assistance vs effort. It depends on the variables involved. I actually entered the jazz/plants prompt just now. While it generates a somewhat viable song, the song is muddy, unexpectedly drops and raises the gain, starts clipping and colliding with the kick, and has pitch issues with the vocals. Correcting these is where the talent and effort come into play, and that's where I disagree on the broad assertion that it's devoid of those. That's just my opinion today, so that could change as the models get better. As far as it being the majority of what is produced, I don't have the data on that, but my anecdotal experience on Spotify does not fall into that category. The songs recommended to me are usually of higher quality.

mentions.text: The main way AI music has been sneaking into my listening is through my Release Radar playlist on Spotify. I wish I could report/give feedback about this, but none of the options for report/feedback are anything relevant. All I can do is right click the "artist", select "dont play this artist", and hope the algorithm will take the hint.

mentions.text: Well, you don't actually own it forever. The thing about physical media is that it degrades and falls apart and ages out of use. You can leave a VHS tape or DVD on your dashboard in the summer and ruin it just as easily as the media itself can become outdated and no longer be easily played on most commercial devices. Do you OWN a VCR? I sure don't. All the VHS tapes my parents owned in 1997 have gone into the trash, and old home movies they have failed to digitized might not be recoverable because of how they've been stored. Even still, the process of watching a VHS tape degraded it as it pulled the tape across the head. Rewinding the tape is how I lost a used copy of Ghostbusters - tape snapped. And given the option, I would rather have a 1080p or 4K digital version than the 330p x 480p resolution VHS tape that I owned in 1988. You get to own the IP for as long as you can care for the media that contains it and as long as you have a way to play it. That's not some evil plan, that's just how things work.
